name: The Lamplighters
theory: The Book is a cage with pages. A cage cannot walk, so it hires a hand. You are the hand. We read the tracks for years and we are sure. Do not ask the cage. A cage says what a cage says.
tells: A dim solar light stands on the path behind you. It was not there this morning.
A truck idles at the end of the road with its lights off. Somebody inside it counts out loud.
A radio clicks twice in the trees. A small voice says a call sign and then too much else.
Someone moved the trail marker one step to the left. It points the right way now.

people.name: Wren Ashby
people.role: Ex-ranger. Keeps the line of lamps. Slow to trust.

people.name: Old Dutch
people.role: Trucker. Moves what needs to move. Likes a joke.

people.name: Pip
people.role: Radio operator, young. Says too much on the air.

hail.text: Halt, {you}. This lamp is a post. I am the post. State how many the Book holds.
The lamp is on, so I am on. Step 1. Stop. Step 2. Show me {lead}.
You carry a lamp from Lamp One. I still check you. A lamp is a promise. It is not a pass.
You lit fewer than 2 fires before we met you at {met}. Pickets remember a cold trail.
You gave the suits your name. I give you mine after the fight. That is the order now.
Message starts. The Bearer is at my lamp and the log is not kind. Message ends. Now we begin.

again.text: You are back after {gap}. The lamp did not move. I did not move. We go again.
{gap} away. I changed the battery twice. Birdie is rested and I am not. Begin.
You make jokes at posts. I heard better ones at the diner. Begin.
You beat 3 of us already. Runners talk. I heard all of it. Begin.

youWin.text: The post is beaten. I log it. Message starts. The Bearer passed lamp and picket. Message ends.
You are better each time. I say that on the air tonight. Lamp One likes a true report.
You won. I still do not wave. Walk on, {you}.

youLose.text: The post holds. Go back to the campfire. Rest {lead}. The lamp stays on for you.
The post holds. NOTE: The path lights go back to the cabin. Follow them. Do not thank me.
You talk hard and fight soft. Reverse that. Then come back.

hail.text: Runner on the line. I carry words between lamps. I have 2 minutes. Use them on a fight.
You ran a message for Sparrow at Tug Fork. So you are a runner too. Runners race. Begin.
You cleared The Pine Plains before we met you. You walked far with no lamp. Runners respect that.
The suits know you. The white coats know you. Everybody runs after the Bearer. I run faster.
You walk with friends. Good. A line is more than one lamp. I still fight one of you.

again.text: {gap} since the last run. I ran 40 miles in that time. You walked back here. Begin.
You are back in {gap}. I did not catch my breath. That is my problem. Begin.
{gap}. The message I carried about you is old news now. Give me a new one.

youWin.text: You win. I carry that up the line. Message starts. The Bearer is quick. Message ends.
You win, and you joke about it. I leave the joke out of the message.
You win. The line likes you, {you}. I say so at every lamp tonight.

youLose.text: I win. I do not have time to enjoy it. Rest {lead} at a campfire.
I win. The Book holds {count}. That is a short line-up and it showed. Come back with more.
I win. The reports on you get worse each week. Change that.

hail.text: This lamp is mine. I clean the panel each day at noon. Now I check the Bearer.
You lit 4 fires before we met you. A fire is a promise. I keep promises for a living.
You had 3 nights out before we met you. You walked on our lights each night. You are welcome.
CAUTION: You carry Reagent 12. Put the bottle on the ground. I do not fight near it.
The suits seize what we shelter now. So I check every stranger twice. This is check 1.
The lamp is on. The count is good. One Bearer, one Book, {count} inside. Begin.

again.text: {gap} since your last check. The lamp ran every night of it. Begin.
{gap}. The panel has dust and so do you. I clean the panel first. Then we begin.
You gave a straight answer last time. I wrote it on the lamp post. Begin.

youWin.text: The check is complete. You pass. A lamp keeper says the count out loud: {count}. Walk on.
You pass. You made a promise at Redwood Creek. Keep it the way I keep this lamp.
You pass, {you}. Take the lit path. I put that one down for people like you.

youLose.text: The check is complete. You fail. Rest. The lamp is here tomorrow and so am I.
You lost to us 2 times now. NOTE: That is not an insult. That is a count.
You fail in the dark. Follow the dim lights to the cabin. Do not follow the bog-light.

hail.text: Night walker. I walk with three tonight. Their names are their own. Show me who walks with you.
The Book holds a hidebehind. We count that. It was behind you. Now it is on a page.
You stood with Lamp One at Annex 9. I walk with one from those cages now. Meet Gus.
We met you first, before the suits and the white coats. We know your first steps. Show me the new ones.
The technician Toby walks with us now. He talks more than Sparrow. He says you are honest. Prove it.
WARNING: The line is cold on you and it gets colder. I do not hold back tonight.

again.text: {gap}. I walked the whole line in that time. You came back to one lamp. Begin.
Back after {gap}. Same night, same walker. Nell remembers you. Begin.
You talk hard to me each time. The ones I walk with do not like it. Begin.

youWin.text: You win. I walk on. NOTE: The Book holds {count}. I say the number so somebody does.
You win, {you}. Lamp One trusts few people. She trusts you. I see why.
You win. You also broke a promise on the ridge. I walk on. I do not wave.

youLose.text: They held. Rest by a campfire. I leave a lamp at the turn for you.
You were new to the dark when we met you. You still are. Rest and come back.
They held this time. Your reports get better. Come back in a day.

posts.line: The Mullica River runs the colour of tea from cedar and iron. Our lamp stands where the water looks like a road.
The tree frog that calls in this cedar swamp lives almost nowhere else. We do not move it. We keep a lamp near it.
The hat at Ong's Hat never came down from the pine. The Office has a form for it. We have a lamp under it.
Skyline Drive runs 105 miles along the crest of the Blue Ridge. We keep one lamp for each bad curve.
The Shay locomotives at Cass haul people up the grade to Bald Knob. A runner rides the last car and carries no radio.
The Silver Bridge fell on December 15, 1967, and 46 people died. The Office files this place. We keep a lamp lit here.
The Wisconsin River is about 430 miles long and carried the log drive to the mills. It carries our messages now.
Motorboats are barred from most of the Boundary Waters. We move by canoe over a thousand lakes and nobody hears.
James MacGillivray first printed Paul Bunyan in 1906 in the Oscoda Press. The Office files it as a rumour. We file it as code.
Cape Flattery is the northwesternmost point of the contiguous United States. The line of lamps ends here and turns around.
Multnomah Falls drops 620 feet. A runner cannot shout over it, so we use a mirror.
A bulldozer crew found enormous footprints here in 1958, and the newspapers named them Bigfoot. The Office makes casts. We rake the road smooth each night.
Lake Erie is the shallowest Great Lake, about 19 metres deep on average. People named its grey serpent Bessie. We approve of plain names.
Lake Michigan lies wholly inside the United States. So no border post reads our lamps on this shore.
Boats fought at Valcour Island on October 11, 1776. The Institute samples the water here. We move ours past them after dark.
The bats leave Carlsbad Caverns at dusk from May to October. The Office counts the bats. We move under the count.
The Joshua tree is a yucca, not a tree, and grows wild only in the Mojave Desert. Our lamp stands next to one. It is also not a tree.
The Herrick brothers made the first mounted jackalopes in Douglas in the 1930s. The Institute measures the mounts. We shelter the live ones.
Many Acadians settled here after they were driven out of Nova Scotia in 1755. This country knows what shelter means. Our lamps do well here.
Marjory Stoneman Douglas called the Everglades a river of grass in her 1947 book. A lamp on a river needs a float.
Reports of the skunk ape come from Florida from the 1960s on. The Institute samples the smell. We walk upwind and keep quiet.
The Ozarks are an eroded plateau, not true mountains. A lamp on high ground shows for miles, so we keep ours dim.
In 1907 fifteen bison came from the Bronx to the Wichita Mountains. The Office files that as a transfer. We call it a good move.
A 1972 film shot around Texarkana made the Fouke monster famous. We do not like cameras. Yours is the exception, for now.

quest.title: First Lamp

hail.text: Stop there, {you}. I am Wren Ashby. Call sign Lamp One. That light at your feet is ours. You walked on our lights all night.
Nobody reached you before us. Good. Then you hear it from us first. I am Lamp One. The path lights are ours.
You gave the suits your name at Apple Pie Hill. It is in a grey file now. I trust a signed name less.
You gave the suits the name Gary. Good. They keep a file on the wrong man. I laughed once. I logged it.
You lit 4 fires before this talk. We counted from the tower road. A fire is a promise to the dark. You keep those.
You lit fewer than 2 fires before this talk. You walked on our lights and gave none back. I note that.
You closed a contract from the sighting board before we met. So the Book already pays its hand. I note that.
You had 3 nights out before I stopped you. Three nights on our lights. Sparrow logged each one, with comments.
Keep your torch low, {you}. It is night and the lamps do the work. I am Lamp One. Stand in the light.
The suits found you. The white coats found you. We are third. Third sees the most. I am Lamp One.

ask.text: The Pinelands reserve is about 1.1 million acres. We light its night paths. The Book holds {count}. I say the number out loud. Why do you carry the Book, {you}?
The Book held 4 kinds before we met. A cage fills fast with a good hand. It holds {count} now. Why do you carry it, {you}?

replies.say: Honestly? It picked me. I'm trying to keep people safe and I don't fully get it yet.

answer.text: That is a plain answer. Plain is rare. Take this lamp. A lamp is a promise. Put it where the path turns.
A plain answer, from a signed name. Take the lamp anyway. A lamp is a promise. I check on promises.

replies.say: Gary carries the snacks, I carry the Book. It's a fair split.

answer.text: I do not log jokes. Sparrow does, on the air, at length. No lamp today. Walk on our lights and think.
Gary again. You use that man like a spare tyre. No lamp today. Walk on our lights and think.

replies.say: It's my Book and my business. Move.

answer.text: Then we check the hand. Otis walks with me. Otis checks you now.

youWin.text: Otis is down. He is fine. You fight clean, {you}. No lamp for hard words. Ask me again one day.
Otis is down in the dark. You did not panic. I log that. Walk on.

youLose.text: Otis held. Rest {lead} at a campfire. Then answer the question again, without the tone.
Otis held. Follow the lamps to the cabin. They are still yours to walk on.

rematch.text: You are back. Otis is rested. The question did not change. I did not change.
{gap} to think. Otis is rested. Show me that you used the time.

quest.log: Wren Ashby stopped me at a path light in Wharton Forest and asked why I carry the Book.

quest.title: Dead Drop

hail.text: Sparrow to {you}. I mean hello. No radios near Green Bank, so we use lamps and mirrors. I talk too much without a radio too.
You talked to the suits at Green Bank first. Say what you told them. Say it slowly. I write with a pencil.
The suits have a listening post at Green Bank. You did not talk to them yet. Good. Keep it that way today.
You carry a lamp from Lamp One. She gave out 3 this year. I asked for one. She said to stop asking.
CAUTION: You carry Reagent 12 from the cold room. I stand over here. The ones we shelter do not like that bottle.
You were away for {gap}. I held this message the whole time. I told nobody. I told Long Haul. Nobody else.
The suits met you first. Lamp One says that is not your fault. She said it twice, so she is not sure.

ask.text: The Tug Fork is a border. A feud ran along it in the 1880s. The Office has a cordon on it now. I need a message carried past. Will you run it?
One suit on the cordon likes you. Agent Quist. That helps. I still need a message carried past the rest. Will you run it?

replies.say: Give it here. I'll walk it past them.

answer.text: Message starts. Lamp 3 is dark. Move Mabel by the river road. Message ends. Do not read it. I just read it to you. Take this ink and go.

replies.say: Can't you just flash it with a mirror? You've got so many mirrors.

answer.text: It is cloudy. A mirror needs sun. That is the whole weakness of the system. Please take the paper.

replies.say: I'm not your mailman, kid.

answer.text: Understood. Sparrow to Lamp One. The Bearer said no. The Bearer also called me kid. I log the kid part.

youWin.text: The paper is through. Sparrow to all lamps. The Bearer runs messages. I said it by mirror, so nobody saw. Thank you.
The paper is through. The suits knew your face and you still passed. Lamp One has to hear this. I tell her twice.

youLose.text: The cordon held. Did they read the paper? Do not answer. Rest {lead}. We try again.
The cordon held. At night they use torches and we see them first. Rest. Try again before dawn.

rematch.text: The cordon is still on the Tug Fork. The paper is still in your pocket. I hope. Go again.
{gap} with our message in your pocket. It said Lamp 3 is dark. Lamp 3 is still dark. Go.

quest.log: Pip asked me to carry a paper message past the Office cordon on the Tug Fork.

quest.title: Tall Tales

hail.text: Long Haul to {you}. Park it. The camps cut the white pine and told tall tales all winter. Those tales are our code book.
The Book holds {count}, and one is a hidebehind. We count it. I say it out loud. One hidebehind, on a page.
The Book holds {count} and no hidebehind. Good count. I like that count. I want to talk about how to keep it.
You lent the white coats a squonk for its tears. A squonk cries enough on its own time. I am not laughing.
You told the suits their oldest asset is wood. Pell guarded a carving for years. That is the best tale this winter.
You joke with me every time. Good. A trucker with no jokes is only a man in a chair.
{gap} since we talked. I drove to Duluth and back. The truck missed you. I did not say I did.
Sparrow says you ran the paper at Tug Fork. Sparrow says a lot. This one I believe.

ask.text: In our code book, the hidebehind means a friend is behind you. Leave the hidebehind alone, {you}. Will you?
The Book holds one already, so that tale is told. Leave the next one alone. Walk easy with yours. Will you?
It is always behind you. So are we. Beat it if you must. Do not let the Book have it. Will you?
Here is the punchline, and it is not a joke. Leave the hidebehind alone. Will you?
You lend out what the Book holds. Do not lend this one to anybody. Leave the hidebehind alone. Will you?
The suits guard a wooden hodag. We guard a tale. Ours is the real one. Leave the hidebehind alone. Will you?

replies.say: Okay. If I can get past it without the Book taking it, I will.

answer.text: Good. That goes in the code book tonight. A new tale. The Bearer who left one alone.
Good. One on a page and no more. I count it again next time. Out loud.

replies.say: Sure. I'll leave it right where it is. Behind me. With you lot.

answer.text: Ha. Log that one, Sparrow. Message starts. The Bearer is funny. Message ends. We have a deal.

replies.say: It's behind me. That makes it mine. Those are the rules.

answer.text: Those are the rules of the cage. Fine. Hazel and Earl walk with me. They want a word.

youWin.text: Hazel and Earl are down. They are fine. They are loggers at heart. You win the word. Think about the tale anyway.
You win. No joke this time. See, I can do it too. Think about the tale.

youLose.text: They held. Rest {lead}. The camps had long winters. I have a long truck. I can wait.
They held. Hard talk, soft line-up. Rest and come back with one of the two fixed.

rematch.text: Hazel and Earl are rested. The coffee is not. Go again.
{gap}. Hazel asked about you. Earl did not. Go again.

quest.log: Old Dutch asked me at the logging camp to leave the hidebehind alone.

quest.title: The Road Shut

hail.text: The road is shut past this stone, {you}. I shut it. The redwoods here are the tallest trees on Earth. People still look at the ground.
The Book holds {count}. One is the giant. So I am too late with my request. Then hold it well.
The Book holds {count} and no giant. Good. Then my request is still in time.
The suits have a copy of your tape. More film brings more people up this road. I shut it harder now.
The grant officer counted your line-up at Mount St. Helens. Everybody counts. We count to keep. She counts to bill.
The reports on you get worse, {you}. I read each one. I still ask you this in person.
{gap} since we spoke. I shut 2 more roads in that time. This is the one that matters.
You still carry my lamp. So I ask you plainly, the way I gave it.

ask.text: One minute of film and some footprints send people up the ridge. We turn them around. Beat the giant if you must. Do not let the Book bind it. Promise?
The Book has one. The request changes. No more from this ridge. Stay on the road and off the footprints. Promise?
The giant on the ridge is ahead of you. Beat it if you must. Do not let the Book bind it. Promise?
Your tape is in an Office drawer now. So promise me two things. No film of the ridge. No giant in the Book. Promise?
The grant officer needs three more specimens. The ridge has one. She can count. So I ask you first. No giant in the Book. Promise?
The line trusts you less each week. A promise can change that. Beat the giant if you must. Do not let the Book bind it. Promise?

replies.say: I promise. If it comes to it, I beat it and walk on. The Book doesn't get it.

answer.text: Logged. A lamp is a promise and so is this. I check it later. I always check.
Logged. No more from this ridge. Hold the one you have well. I check both.

replies.say: I'll ask the Book. It usually says no, but it says it politely.

answer.text: The cage does not get a vote. You do. I wait for a real answer. I am good at waiting.

replies.say: I don't make promises about things I haven't met yet.

answer.text: That is honest and it is not enough. Then you do not pass on words. Ruth, June and Otis walk with me.

youWin.text: They are down. You pass. NOTE: The request stands. A fight does not answer it. Your hand does.
They are down. You pass. The Book has the one. Do not bring it up this road.

youLose.text: They held. The road stays shut. Rest {lead}. Then come back and talk to me.
They held. You said no and then you lost. Think about which one to change.

rematch.text: The road is still shut. Ruth, June and Otis are rested. So is the question.
{gap}. Nobody passed in that time. The road is still shut. Go again.

quest.log: Wren Ashby shut the road at Redwood Creek and asked me for a promise about the giant.

quest.title: Night Boat

hail.text: Sparrow to {you}. Lake Champlain is about 120 miles long. We move them over it after dark. I must not say where. It is the east dock.
Message starts. The safe house at the east dock is empty. The suits came first. Protocol QUIET. They took Mabel. Message ends. Sorry. I am not calm.
You took Specimen HI-031 out of the Institute cold room. We shelter it now. It has a name now. It is Clyde. It eats well.
We have a tip from inside the Office. A suit with a scrapbook. Lamp One says not to say Quist on the air. I said Quist.
{gap} since we last talked. I counted. Lamp One says I count the wrong things.
You ran my paper at Tug Fork. So I asked for you by call sign. You do not have one. I can fix that.
It is dark, so the boat is ready. Do not use your torch on the dock. The lamps show the way to the water.
You make jokes when I talk. I like it. Lamp One says I must not like it on the air.

ask.text: The boat goes tonight with three passengers. They are afraid of the water. Will you ride with them, {you}?
Lamp One plans a raid on Annex 9 to get ours back. First the last three cross tonight. Will you ride with them?

replies.say: I'll ride. Tell me where to sit and what not to touch.

answer.text: Sit in the middle. Touch nothing. Lamp One keeps a plan for Annex 9 in a drawer. You are in the drawer now. Forget I said that.
Sit in the middle. Touch nothing. The raid plan has your name on it now. Lamp One wrote it herself.

replies.say: Do the passengers get life jackets, or just me?

answer.text: One of them is a fish with fur. It does not need one. You get the orange one. Welcome to the plan for Annex 9.

replies.say: I'm not smuggling anything across a border lake at night.

answer.text: It is not smuggling. It is moving. The manual has a different page for each. Sparrow out. I mean, fine.

youWin.text: The boat is across. The passengers are calm. Sparrow to all lamps. I say nothing. I say almost nothing. The Bearer did it.
The Office launch turned back. The boat is across. Three are safe. Lamp One wants you at White Sands. I wrote it on my hand.

youLose.text: The boat turned back. Nobody is hurt. Pearl is seasick. Rest {lead}. We try again in the next dark hour.
The Office launch held the channel. We turned back. They did not get the passengers. Rest. We go again.

rematch.text: The boat is ready again. The lake did not get shorter. Go.
{gap} on the dock. The passengers learned your name. Go again.

quest.log: Pip asked me to ride the night boat over Lake Champlain with three passengers.

quest.title: Annex Raid

hail.text: White Sands is the largest gypsum dune field in the world. White ground shows everything. So we go at night and we go once.
You know the plan from the lake. Sparrow told you more than I wrote. Step 1. Cut the cordon. Step 2. Open the cages. Step 3. Leave.
You are not in the plan. You did not ride the boat. I add you in pencil. Do what I say when I say it.
You stood inside Annex 9 already. Draw the rooms. Here is a stick. The sand is the paper.
A suit left the side door off the latch. I do not say the name. Sparrow said it already.
The white coats put a meter next to the Book. It read one thing each time. I do not need a meter. It is a cage.
The suits took 9 from our safe houses. I know each name. Tonight I say each name at a cage door.
I do not trust you much, {you}. The log says why. Tonight I need hands. Yours work.
{gap} since we spoke. The cages were full the whole time. I counted the days for them.

ask.text: The Book holds {count}. The Annex holds more, in cages with numbers. Which way do you go in, {you}?
You saw the rooms. So you pick the door. Which way do you go in, {you}?

replies.say: Quiet. Side door, low, behind you. I do what you say.

answer.text: Correct. Stay on my left. When I say a name, open that cage. Take this ink for the cordon.

replies.say: Have we tried knocking? Agents love a knock. There's probably a form.

answer.text: There is a form. It is Form 9-C. We do not fill it in. Stay on my left and stay quiet.

replies.say: Front door. Loud. Let them see who's doing it.

answer.text: WARNING: Loud gets cages moved before we reach them. You go in the front. I go in the side. Do not make me come for you.

youWin.text: The cordon is down. The cages are open. I said each name. Message starts. Annex 9 is empty. The line holds. Message ends.
The cordon is down. The plan held, Sparrow and all. The cages are open. Nine names, nine doors. Move.
The cages are open. The suits come back to an empty store. Pell has to write that up. I want a copy.

youLose.text: The cordon held. Fall back to the dunes. White ground shows everything, so keep low. We go again.
The front door held. I said so. Fall back. Next time stay on my left.

rematch.text: The Annex is still full. The cordon is still up. Stay on my left. Go.
{gap}. The cages were full for all of it. Go now.

quest.log: Wren Ashby led a night raid on Annex 9 from the dunes at White Sands.

quest.title: Smugglers' Bay

hail.text: Long Haul to {you}. Jean Lafitte's smugglers worked these bays in the early 1800s. We work them now. We move better cargo.
You told the suits where our boats go. They burned the cache. I do not have a joke for that. Get in the boat.
You are here before the suits. The bay is quiet. I like a quiet bay. Help me keep it that way.
The technician Toby is on one of my boats. He left the white coats. He talks the whole trip. He is good with a rope.
The line runs cold on you, {you}. I read the log on the drive down. Today you get a boat and no coffee.
The suits came in a pirogue. You sent them wrong or you stood in the way. Either one buys you coffee.
The ones from Annex 9 came through here last week. Each has a name now. One has your name. It bites.
Here comes the funny one. Good. The bay needs it today.
{gap} since we talked. The truck is parked. I drive a boat here. Badly.

ask.text: A boat of suits is in the channel with their assets. We hold the bay or we lose it. Where do you stand, {you}?
Six of ours are in cages on the Office boat. This is a rescue. You sent them here. Where do you stand?
One scout boat came ahead of the suits. It has three assets and a clipboard. Where do you stand, {you}?

replies.say: In the bow, with you. Point me at them.

answer.text: Good. The bow it is. Keep {lead} low until I say.
Fine. The bow. Fix what you broke. Then we talk.

replies.say: Do I get a hat? Lafitte's people had hats.

answer.text: No hat. There is a bucket. You can wear the bucket. Welcome aboard.
No hat. No bucket. Not today. Get in.

replies.say: This is between you and the suits. I'm just walking through.

answer.text: Nobody walks through a bay. It is water. The suits are in the channel anyway. Get in or swim.

youWin.text: The bay is ours. Long Haul to all lamps. Bay held. The Bearer stood in the bow. Out.
Six cages are open. Six names are back on the line. You fixed it. I am still sore. Give me a week.
The scout boat is gone. The suits arrive to an empty bay. I left them a bucket.
Bay held. Toby cheered and fell in. He is fine. He is still talking.

youLose.text: They hold the channel. Pull back to the cypress. Rest {lead}. We go again on the tide.
They still have six of ours. Rest fast, {you}. That is an order.

rematch.text: The suits are still in the channel. The tide is right. Get in the boat.
{gap}. The bay waited. Bays are good at that. Get in the boat.
Six of ours are still in cages. I counted them each hour. Get in the boat.

quest.log: Old Dutch and I held the bay at Barataria against an Office boat.

quest.title: The Long Haul

hail.text: Route 66 was commissioned in 1926. Long Haul parked his truck on it. This is the end of our line, {you}. I walk with four.
We met you first, at {met}, at a path light. I gave you a question then. Tonight I give you my answer.
You made a promise at Redwood Creek. The Book holds the giant. The promise is broken. I say it out loud so you hear it.
You made a promise at Redwood Creek. The Book holds {count} and no giant. The promise is kept. I checked. I always check.
The Office is closed. The Institute is closed. We are the last ones behind you. Their leftovers walk with me now.
You held the bay with Long Haul. He tells it at every truck stop. I heard it 6 times.
You sent the suits to Barataria and the cache burned. You helped after. Both are in the log. I read both.
The log on you is long and mostly good. I did not expect that at Wharton Forest.
The log on you is long and mostly bad. I read it twice to be fair.
{gap} since we spoke. I walked the whole line once more. Every lamp was on.
You talk hard to me. You did from the start. I respect a steady signal.

ask.text: The Book holds {count}. I say the number one last time. What happens when the cage is full, {you}?
You still carry my lamp. The Book holds {count}. What happens when the cage is full, {you}?

replies.say: I don't know. But I'm the one carrying it, so I'll be there when it happens.

answer.text: That is the first true answer anybody gave me about the Book. Stand ready. My four want to know you too.

replies.say: Then I guess it needs a second volume. Gary's already picked a title.

answer.text: I do not log jokes. I logged that one. Stand ready.

replies.say: Ask the Book yourself. You've followed it long enough.

answer.text: I do not talk to a cage. I talk to the hand. The hand has its back up. Stand ready.

youWin.text: My four are down. They are fine. Verdict. You carry a cage and you are not a jailer. I do not understand it. I log it.
Verdict. The log says you gave more than you took. The line is yours to walk, {you}. Every lamp. Lamp One out.
Verdict. The log is even. Half promise, half trouble. The lamps stay on for you. I keep watching.
Verdict. The log is cold. You beat us and you did not join us. Walk on our lights. Do not ask for one.
Verdict. You kept the ridge promise and the log is good. Here is a second lamp. I never gave two before.
Verdict. You beat us and you broke the ridge promise. The lamps stay on. They are for everybody. That is all you get.

youLose.text: My four held. That is not the verdict. Rest {lead} at a campfire. Come back and finish it.
My four held. The lamps on Route 66 go to a cabin. Follow them. Come back in daylight. I am here.
My four held. I am not surprised. Change my mind.

rematch.text: The truck is still parked. My four are rested. The verdict waits. Stand ready.
{gap}. Long Haul kept the engine warm. Stand ready.

quest.log: Wren Ashby and the four who walk with her met me at Old Dutch's truck on Route 66.

mythic-bound.text: The Book bound {mythic}. The count went up by one. We heard it at every lamp. I say the number: {count}.
The Book bound {mythic}. That is the giant, and you made a promise. I say the number anyway: {count}.

mythic-loose.text: You beat {mythic} and left it loose. That is the correct procedure. A runner carried the news to nine lamps.

hunt-closed.text: You closed a contract from a sighting board. The cage pays its hand. We note the payment.

binds-8.text: The Book holds 8 kinds now. I say it out loud. Eight. Somebody has to hear the number.

binds-16.text: The Book holds 16 kinds now. Sixteen. Sparrow said it on the air and then said sorry.

long-away.text: You were gone 3 days or more. The lamps ran each night anyway. A lamp is a promise.
You were gone a long time. Sparrow asked about you each night. I asked once.

office-file.text: You gave the Office your name. It is in a grey drawer now. We use call signs for a reason.

office-gary.text: The Office has a file on Gary. Gary does not know. Do not tell Gary. This is the best news all month.

protocol-quiet.text: WARNING: Protocol QUIET is active. The Office seizes what we shelter. Message starts. All lamps dim. Move by night only. Message ends.

cache-burned.text: The cache at Barataria burned. The Office knew where to go. We know who told them. Long Haul wants a word.

quist-turned.text: A suit with a scrapbook asked what the Book does with them. That suit leaves doors open now. We do not say the name.

office-closed.text: The Office is closed. The grey suits went home with two forms each. We put a lamp at their door. It is a good door.

sample-given.text: You put {lead} on the Institute scale. They have a number for it now. We have a name for it. A name is better.

reagent-taken.text: CAUTION: You carry Reagent 12. The ones we shelter turn away from that bottle. Keep it shut near our lamps.

squonk-lent.text: You lent a squonk to the Institute for its tears. Get it back. Then tell it you are sorry. It cries. It always cries.

specimen-freed.text: You took a specimen out of the cold room before the Office came. We shelter it now. It has a name and a blanket.

toby-out.text: The technician Toby left the Institute. He is at one of our posts. He labels our lamps. We let him.

institute-closed.text: The Institute is closed. The grant ran out. Vale kept the notebooks. We shelter the ones she measured.

rumours: Diner cook: Those little solar lights on the trail? Not the county's. I asked. County thought they were ours.
Clerk: Old fella in a truck buys forty batteries every Tuesday. Pays cash. Tells me a joke. Same joke.
Night manager: There's a kid on channel 9 who says 'message ends' and then keeps going for ten minutes.
Diner cook: Ranger lady comes in, orders coffee, counts everybody in the room out loud, leaves. Tips well.
Clerk: Somebody keeps buying up the tall-tale books. All of them. Says they're for work.
Night manager: Truck in the back lot had something in it humming. Driver said it was the fridge. The fridge had a name.
